page: Hetzner Cloud cpx51 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured within the Regular Purpose family and managed under the QEMU hypervisor. The hardware deployment delivers 16 shared vCPUs derived from AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, with 16 physical cores mapped at a single thread per core. The instance provides 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Physical caching is distributed across 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Acceleration is focused strictly on CPU-bound and vector extensions such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, without discrete GPU hardware. Fast storage is directly attached via a 360 GB NVMe SSD, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Performance assessments reflect the shared CPU infrastructure. Single-threaded capability is constrained, with single-core stress-ng tests rating in the bottom 10 percent at 771.59 points and Geekbench single-core registering 1466.0. In contrast, multi-core capacity scales effectively across the 16 execution contexts, achieving an average-tier multi-core Geekbench score of 11,375.0, a PassMark CPU rating of 29,689.83, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 55.38 GB/sec. Memory subsystems register 86.13 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 53.91 GB/sec in write operations. High-throughput scenarios such as Redis caching achieve 30.41 million SET operations per second, alongside static web serving delivery of 18.81 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cpx51 instance maximizes core density and storage capacity without the overhead associated with dedicated-core instances or specialized enterprise GPU tiers. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and shared CPU architecture necessitate careful consideration for jitter-sensitive latency workloads. However, the abundant core count combined with 360 GB of bundled NVMe storage makes this instance technically fitting for parallelized compilation pipelines, multi-threaded data transformations, horizontal web servers, and development or staging environments.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx51 is a virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor running on the x86_64 architecture under the QEMU hypervisor. The instance provisions 16 shared vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz alongside 31.0 GB of memory, representing approximately 1.95 GB per core. Local storage is included as a 360 GB NVMe SSD, while dedicated graphics acceleration is not provided. Benchmark results place single-core performance in lower percentiles, but multi-threaded metrics reach expected mid-range tiers, illustrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,375 and multi-core stress-ng throughput of 12,463.46. Memory operations and caching throughput align with mainstream tier distributions, supporting redis operations of 30.41 million sets per second and static web transfer rates of 18.81 GB/sec. Given its shared CPU model and 1:2 memory ratio, cpx51 provides dense multi-threaded capacity for distributed web serving, continuous integration builds, container clusters, and background batch tasks.
